name: Art Gallery of Nova Scotia
known: Corporate supporters: BMO Financial Group supports Free Access Thursday Nights (AGNS plan-your-visit page); the business-support page lists TD under "Current Supporters" for the TD Assistant Curatorial Fellowship and shows further supporter logos, including Scotia Investments and CKF.
Posts annual reports from 2013-14 to 2025-26 and financial statements back to 2011-12; the 2024-25 report names supporters and the board page names directors.

name: Art Gallery of Hamilton
known: The incite Foundation for the Arts sponsored the 2024 "Directors Collect: 110 Years" exhibition, Free Thursdays (with RBC), education and library pass programmes;
The 2024 board is chaired by Gary Graham and includes two Hamilton city councillors;
Shelley Falconer is president and CEO.

name: Musée d'art de Joliette
known: Governance: a board of directors chaired by Emmanuel Préville-Ratelle.
Annie Gauthier is director general and chief curator (2025 annual report).

Fondation du Musée d'art de Joliette: granted $644,300 to the museum in 2024-2025, of which 35% went to educational programmes, 23% to exhibitions, 22% to conservation and 20% to temporary exhibitions and events (2025 annual report).

name: Galerie de l'UQAM
known: French Wikipedia lists Louise Déry as director.

name: MAC Montréal
known: Museum of contemporary art founded by the Quebec government in 1964, described as the first institution in Canada devoted exclusively to contemporary art (Wikipedia).
Director general Stéphan La Roche signed the 2024-25 report on 9 July 2025.
Claudie Imbleau-Chagnon chairs the board (2024-25 annual report).

The museum became a société d'État on 16 May 1984 under the Loi sur les musées nationaux, with a board of directors in charge; before that it reported directly to the Ministry (2024-25 annual report).

The Foundation's 20 million dollar campaign "L'art de transformer", launched in April 2024 and co-chaired by Claudine and Stephen Bronfman, had passed half its goal; private gifts complete the public investment in the rebuild (2024-25 annual report).

name: PHI Foundation
known: Founded by Phoebe Greenberg, who was inspired by the Fondation Cartier.
Wikipedia says she is the daughter of Irving Greenberg, a co-founder of Minto Group in 1955.

name: The Polygon Gallery
known: The Audain Foundation also made an investment in support of the Audain Chief Curator.
Posts annual reports for 2021 to 2024; the 2024 report holds financial statements, a named donor list for 2024 and the board of directors.

name: Owens Art Gallery

name: Remai Modern
